key_insight: Rubric-guided large language models can approximate expert grading of Linux/bash exam answers, but accuracy drops as question complexity moves from simple retrieval to advanced system tasks.
engineering_relevance: The study offers a practical blueprint for scalable AI-assisted grading in computing education, helping instructors triage which questions can be auto-graded and which need human review.
method: Compared four frontier LLMs: GPT, Claude Opus, Gemini, and GLM.
Tested two prompts: a minimal baseline and a rubric-enhanced version.
Used a four-level cognitive taxonomy spanning L1 information retrieval to L4 advanced system management.
evidence_signal: On 1,200 real student responses graded by three expert instructors, Gemini 3.0 Pro with rubric prompting reached the best agreement with humans (ICC(3,1)=0.888, MAE=0.10).
watch_item: Performance falls at higher taxonomy levels, so complex or ambiguous shell tasks still require careful human oversight.
paper_title: Automated grading of Linux/bash examinations using large language models: a four-level cognitive taxonomy approach
